The Future Seen from the Past
You can talk about an event that was in the future at a particular point in the past. You use the past tenses of the verb forms you would normally use to talk about the future.
You can express the future as a future event seen from now, or as a future event supposed to happen at a certain point in the past.

Real Conditional: Expressing Possible Future Events
You use the Real conditional with If clauses to exchange opinions about possible future outcomes.
You use the Real Conditional to say it's possible that you will or will not do something. In that condition, something else may, may not will or will not happen.
The parts of the sentence are divided into two clauses: the If clause and the Condition clause.
You use if ... happen to, or if ... should happen to to express an outcome that may be possible, but not very likely.
If you should happen to have something to say, you want to tell everyone, right?
If they happen to retweet, thank them, right?
If they don't happen to be interested in the minutiae of your life every 10 minutes, they should stop following you right?
So if they should happen to hang on your every word, tweet them well.

images.text: If you should happen to have something to say, you want to tell everyone, right?  If they happen to retweet, thank them, right?  If they don't happen to be interested in the minutiae of your life every 10 minutes, they should stop following you right? So if they should happen to hang on your every word, tweet them well.

If you don't happen to be interested in Twitter, stop here.
I do follow Twitter. I spend time gleaning tweets for scoops or enlightenment on things less talked about. I deduce, garner, extract what I can and move on. I don't follow the power users. I myself have an account, but rarely speak. If I did, it would go something like this:

5:00 a.m. Sitting under my Sad Light Therapy lamp. I wasn't going to complain but the sun won't be back this early for months!
6:00 a.m. Couldn't get the first streetcar because I was standing in line for coffee.
6:30 a.m. Subway decided it would hold us hostage for an extra half hour today.
7:20 a.m. Commute was so slow I would have been better off walking!
7:40 a.m. It was announced that the servers would be down all day and we should work from home.
7:50 a.m. I heard on my way out that we were all to be moved to a new office space in a week. Ummm ...
8:30 a.m. Was about to leave the office when I was sidetracked by my boss wanting to chat ...
9:30 a.m. Texts were sent out to all of us to come back to the office - crashed server back online ...
10:00 a.m. Missed the streetcar because I was standing in line for coffee ...
